I recently moved to this area, so I chose a clinic that was close and had many reviews, but I was disappointed in several ways. Let me list them point by point:

1. Parking is difficult because it's on Phatthanakan Road, which isn't very wide. Motorcycles are recommended; you can usually find parking on the sidewalk.
2. The clinic itself is very cramped. You can see the operating room from behind the counter.
3. I wish they would renovate and improve the decor to make it look newer and cleaner. The place is quite old, which made it feel very unrelaxing (and even a little scary).
4. The atmosphere in the treatment room was unpleasant. There were many staff members who were constantly chatting (I personally thought they were family members or close friends because they talked about things other than work). This made me feel like an outsider.
And point 5, an experience I'll remember forever. While waiting for my treatment, an older man came out of the treatment room after having his teeth cleaned, groaning and complaining, "It hurts like hell!" A little later, he said, "It hurts so much!" <First unsettling moment.> The examination room required several X-rays before they were approved (probably because the staff were inexperienced). The atmosphere in the examination room <Second unsettling moment.> Then, once I entered the treatment room... I think it was the dentist or his assistant who told the housekeeper, a Burmese woman, to wipe the blood off the bandage (I'm pretty sure it was blood from before – the uncle who complained of pain). <My third moment of unease.> When the actual dental work started, it hurt so much. Even just scaling was painful. There was blood everywhere, even though I usually don't have much tartar buildup because I always floss regularly.

Finally, I want to advise everyone, no matter what service you're using, to read reviews carefully and check the credibility of the reviewer.
